video.title: The Most Passive Online Business No One Talks About

summary: The video explains how to find and launch niche directory websites by spotting service searches, weak local listings, and recommendation requests on Google, Facebook, Reddit, Craigslist, and YouTube. The host presents directories as a way to organize provider information and earn through ads, affiliate links, paid placement, or lead generation. He recommends five niches: rural mobile dog groomers, wedding vendors outside major platforms, Medicaid therapists who answer email, venues that allow outside food, and commercial kitchen rentals. His launch plan is to validate demand, list ten providers, build a simple prototype, soft launch it, and then test monetization.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; no guest is identified.

ideas.name: Niche directory websites
ideas.one_liner: Organize service providers around a specific search need and monetize the directory with ads, affiliate clicks, paid placement, or leads.
ideas.business_model: Advertising, affiliate commissions, paid listings, and lead generation.
ideas.customer: People searching for a provider or service, and providers seeking visibility or leads.
ideas.problem: Search results can be cluttered with outdated, weak, or irrelevant listings, while niche needs and filters are poorly organized.
ideas.offer: A clean directory of relevant providers with useful filters and accurate details.

pricing.model: Featured listings, ads, affiliate commissions, and lead generation.

price_points.label: Suggested price range for basic featured listings

pricing.notes: Other monetization routes are mentioned without prices.

acquisition_channels.details: Find long-tail searches and weak search results, then build a focused directory that can rank for the niche.

quote.text: Directories can rank stupidly fast, especially if you're targeting the right keywords.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Inspect map listings for keyword-stuffed business names, weak websites, missing lead forms, and service gaps.
Post a prototype in a relevant local group and research recommendation requests and comments.
The host suggests DMing listed providers to ask whether they want a listing or featured placement. In the UK, unsolicited marketing DMs to individuals and sole traders require consent.

ideas.delivery: A website presents listings, details, and filters, then directs users to providers or captures leads. The host describes the founder as organizing information rather than performing the listed service.
unit_economics_claims: The host says directories can earn through advertising, affiliate clicks, paid placement, and lead generation, but gives no revenue or cost figures.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated; the host says a directory can be live within 24 to 48 hours, which is not a claim about first revenue

acquisition.how: SEO research, content publishing, and analytics can be automated, with human review of the niche and search intent.

onboarding.how: Forms and data imports can collect listings, but a person should check provider details and permission.

delivery.how: Directory pages, filters, and provider links can run in software; periodic human checks are needed for stale or incorrect data.

billing.how: Subscriptions and invoices for featured listings can run through payment software with occasional review.

support.how: Agents can handle routine listing questions, but disputes and accuracy requests may need a person.

uk_applicability.notes: The directory model works in the UK. The founder must follow UK privacy and marketing rules, particularly for unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals and sole traders.

risks: A weak competitor in search results does not prove that a directory will attract users or paying providers.
Listings can become stale or inaccurate; validate demand across more than one source and check details.
The host suggests using scraped information and listing providers without permission during prototyping. Check platform terms, privacy obligations, and listing rights before doing this in the UK.
Unsolicited marketing DMs, emails, or texts to UK individuals and sole traders may require prior consent.

quotes.text: Second, directory websites can make money like a vending machine. Set it up once and it starts generating ad revenue, affiliate clicks, paid placement, lead genen forms, whatever you want
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Find long-tail directory opportunities in search
steps: Search Google for 'near me' and inspect results beyond the first few pages for unusual service terms.
Search for directory pages with a niche term and inspect whether current results are outdated or poorly organized.
Use Ahrefs and Keywords Everywhere to check search volume and competition, then inspect the actual search results yourself.
Treat weak competitors as a signal to investigate, not proof that a directory will succeed.

quote.text: Sometimes you just got to go there yourself to get a feel for it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use maps and provider questions to find filter gaps
steps: Search Google Maps for a specific local service and inspect business names and websites for keyword stuffing, weak design, missing photos, few reviews, or missing lead forms.
Check provider questions and answers for repeated questions about hours, languages, insurance, or service availability.
Use filters such as open now, mobile, kid-friendly, and languages spoken only when there is evidence that users want them.
Verify listing details before publishing them.

quote.text: Each question is a filter that people care about. And you can add all of these filters to your directory, or you can make a directory out of one filter entirely.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Mine Facebook groups for recurring requests
steps: Find active local or interest groups where members ask for recommendations.
Search group posts for phrases such as 'looking for', 'recommend', or 'anyone know a good'.
Read comments as well as the original post to see whether requests are answered and which filters matter.
Save recurring requests, comments, and engagement in a simple Google Doc or Sheet.
Ask group members what filters and budget would matter to them, then use the answers to shape a prototype.

quote.text: The gold is really in the comments there. You don't even really need to guess what filters to add to these searches.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Mine Reddit for unmet local needs
steps: Choose subreddits where people ask for recommendations or plan events.
Search for phrases such as 'recommend a', 'anyone know a good', and 'where to get a'.
Read comment threads for repeat unanswered questions, frustration, and links to poor-quality alternatives.
Sort posts by time period to spot recurring questions.
Use Google site search to find Reddit threads when Reddit's own search is inconvenient.

quote.text: The comments are where people are having difficulty finding answers to their questions.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Validate and launch a simple directory
steps: Choose a niche with repeated search or recommendation evidence and identify the filters people ask for.
Find ten real providers using sources such as Google Maps, Reddit, Yelp, and Facebook; collect name, city, link, and one or two useful details.
Build a minimum viable directory with a simple tool such as Carrd, Softr, Notion, Airtable, or Tally.
Ask whether a visitor can solve the problem faster than with Google.
Soft launch the page in a relevant local group and test provider interest.
Add featured listings, upgrades, affiliate links, or lead forms only after the prototype is real.

quote.text: The question I'm asking you is, can someone land on your site and solve their problem faster than Google? That's the bar you're trying to beat.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Start with simple research and record patterns
steps: Use Keywords Everywhere for quick keyword context and the free BuiltWith browser extension to inspect weak competitors' technology.
Save useful posts, search results, filters, domains, and competitor tools in a Google Sheet, Airtable, Google Doc, or notes app.
Track niches across sources and move a repeated, well-supported request onto a build-next list.
Do not buy expensive research software before knowing that its features are needed.

quote.text: None of these tools really matter if you don't execute.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner
